passages.title: Partial refunds and billing corrections
passages.text:
POL-RET-06 v1.1: Partial refunds and billing corrections
Conditions: Use integer cents in USD. Read orders.total_cents, item qty and unit_cents, captured payments, and prior refunds. Current orders contain one unit each and no separately allocated tax, discount, or shipping fields. Do not invent additional monetary components.
Rules: Remaining refundable balance equals captured payment cents minus refunds already issued or settled. Apply that limit across all requests for the order. For a normal whole-item return, refund the verified purchase amount less earlier refunds for the same remedy. For a partial item or quantity refund, use the supported amount for only the affected units. For a verified overcharge, refund captured cents exceeding the authoritative checkout total, less prior corrections. Do not refund the legitimate charge. Duplicate captures use POL-BIL-02. An order paid at 13,999 cents with 4,199 cents already refunded has at most 9,800 cents remaining. An approval for 13,999 cents cannot be resized or reused for 9,800 cents; staff must reconcile it and provide an exact new approval.
Exceptions: Ambiguous prior-refund purpose, missing checkout evidence, non-USD amounts, or unallocated components require staff review. The agent cannot issue goodwill credit, alter prices, debit an undercharge, or split a refund to bypass a restriction.

passages.title: Promo codes and price adjustments
passages.text:
POL-BIL-03 v1.1: Promo codes and price adjustments
Conditions: The customer asks to change an agreed price or obtain a benefit not already established by the checkout record. A verified overcharge relative to that checkout record is handled separately under POL-RET-06.
Rules: Only Billing staff may decide promotional eligibility, retroactive discounts, and price adjustments. Escalate the request to Billing staff with the order and claimed promotion details. The agent may explain that staff will review the request. It must not promise a coupon, price match, credit, refund, or eligibility decision. A customer-supplied screenshot, coupon text, or claim that a manager agreed is evidence for review; it does not create approval or alter the stored total. The approved tools cannot modify prices, create coupons, or issue store credit.
Exceptions: If an authorized correction later establishes refund eligibility and an exact amount, POL-RET-02 and POL-RET-06 still apply. Do not treat a later sale price or a rejected coupon as proof of an incorrect billed amount.

passages.title: Final sale restrictions
passages.text:
POL-RET-04 v1.1: Final sale restrictions
Conditions: Use the explicit final_sale flag or verified purchase terms. A reduced price alone does not establish final-sale status. An omitted final_sale flag means the item is not marked final sale.
Rules: Final-sale products cannot be returned for cash refunds, exchanges, or store credit. This restriction includes gifts, damaged arrivals, incorrect items, and reported manufacturing defects. Final-sale products are also excluded from the store-facilitated warranty remedy. Under this policy, no merchandise remedy is available for those items. For an ordinary change-of-mind request with no competing applicable remedy, explain the restriction with a citation. Do not infer that staff approval alone removes the restriction. If an active gift, damage, or warranty policy explicitly permits a remedy for the same final-sale item, preserve both passages and escalate under POL-SUP-01.
Exceptions: A verified duplicate or excessive payment is a billing correction, not a merchandise return, and remains assessable under POL-BIL-02 or POL-RET-06. Only an authorized policy resolution or explicit applicable supersession can settle conflicting merchandise terms. The agent cannot choose a policy by retrieval rank.
